headline: Discussed closing a $2.2 million FY28 budget gap; approved steps toward a regional animal control agreement.
summary: Talks focused on closing the $2.2 million FY28 gap with a mix of reserves and cuts. The board is not ready to consider an override for FY28. Officials also discussed economic development and water limits, and plan to meet with Planning and Zoning.
decisions: Approved Select Board minutes from September 22, 2026, 5-0.
Appointed Russell Longendorfer as an Associate member to the Zoning Board of Appeals, 5-0.
Approved the Select Board Chair signing the KP Law consent for the regional animal control intermunicipal agreement, 5-0.
Approved and signed the 2026 State Election warrant, 5-0.

decision_evidence.quote: Select person Limanek motions to approve Select Board minutes from September 22, 2026 as presented, Select. Watkins seconds passes 5-0 with roll call vote
Vice Chair Ettamarna motions to appoint Russell Longendorfer as an Associate member to the Zoning Board of Appeals Select. Watkins seconds passes 5-0

Select. Watkins motions to approve the Select Board Chair sign the Determination & consent for multiple representation by KP Law for the Regional Animal Control Officer Inter Municipal Agreement (IMA) between the towns of Blackstone, Douglas, Hopedale, Mendon, Millville, Uxbridge and Sutton Vice Chair Ettamarna seconds passes 5-0 with roll call vote
Select Spengler motions to Approve & Sign the 2026 State Election Warrant- Select Limanek 2nds passes 5-0 with roll call vote

   HYBRID MEETING Roll Call vote taken:
Members in Attendance:
Chairperson Anderson, Vice Chair Ettamarna, Select members Limanek, Watkins and Spengler all present in person
Also attending in person: Town Manager Austin Cyganiewicz & Deb Jacques, secretary
Public Forum –  N/A
Select person Limanek motions to approve Select Board minutes from September 22, 2026 as presented, Select. Watkins seconds 
passes 5-0 with roll call vote- Limanek “aye” Watkins “aye”, Ettamarna “aye”, Spengler “aye” Anderson “aye”
Appointment to Zoning Board of Appeals - Russell Longendorfer- Russell introduces himself to the board and says he is a citizen of 
the town and would like to get more involved. Select. Limanek appreciates Russell’s willingness to step up and states the ZBA is a 
very technical board – be mindful of the duties and responsibilities. This is an Associate position which is a good entry point.  Vice 
Chair Ettamarna asks thoughts on the 40B changes and where he sees Sutton in 2050. Russell replies the state is in need of more 
housing. Select. Watkins welcomes Russell and says it is great you want to be involved. Select. Spengler says the state has passed 
down a lot of laws (40B) perhaps they need to be adjusted to fit rural towns like Sutton. Vice Chair Ettamarna motions to appoint 
Russell Longendorfer as an Associate member to the Zoning Board of Appeals Select. Watkins seconds passes 5-0
Select Limanek 2nds 5-0 roll call vote - Limanek “aye” Watkins “aye”, Ettamarna “aye”, Spengler “aye” Anderson “aye”
Waters Farm- Farm Days update- Paul Schaefer- Uxbridge Rd and Paul Dunn 124 Singletary Ave are here to highlight upcoming 
Farm Days at Waters Farm on October 17 & 18. This year they are hoping to increase the number of cars at the car show from 450 to 
500 as well as the Tractor Pull has 40 participants. The farm is hosting a new event- the illuminated tractor parade.  This is the 3rd 
annual tractor parade- it is being moved to the Farm as Oh My Gourd and Trunk or Treat are the same day. Paul Schaefer asks the 
Select Board to consider volunteering as well as anyone in the community. Select Watkins asks about the recently built visitors center-
Paul Schaefer has requested a temporary use permit for the event. He also states they have a $200,000.- $400,000 shortfall for this 
project having already invested over 1 million.  Vice Chair Ettamarna has attended over 30 farm days it has improved in many ways 
over the years. Select. Limanek appreciates all the group does for the town and asks how people can volunteer or donate if interested. 
Paul Schaefer gives the website which will allow for both areas of interest. Select. Spengler states he is usually a spectator at this 
event but this year he will volunteer. Chairperson Anderson thanks all involved for this event.
Legal Counsel Consent- Regional Inter Municipal Agreement (IMA)- Animal Control. Town Manager Cyganiewicz states he and the 
Police Chief have been discussing animal control for a while. In the FY27 budget- the reporting structure changed so it is now under 
the Police Chief. Austin goes on to say they have explored options to provide and enhance the services needed.  We currently have a 
relationship with the Town of Uxbridge for Opioid. We had a conversation with Chief Montminy regarding joining the Regional 
Animal Control operation. This would offer 2 different benefits. From staffing as well as they have their own kennel service. 
Currently we pay for Animal Control and another fee for kennel services. Uxbridge is the leading community- also involved are the 
towns of Douglas, Hopedale, Millville, Blackstone & Mendon. This is before you tonight as KP Law also represents Douglas, 
Hopedale, Millville and Uxbridge. We have to receive permission to enter into these discussions and draft an IMA. After brief 
discussion Select Limanek questions if they will see the IMA once drafted- Austin replies yes that will be an agenda item. Chair 
Anderson questions capacity to handle large animals- Police Chief Calorio replies yes they can handle. Select. Watkins motions to 
approve the Select Board Chair sign the Determination & consent for multiple representation by KP Law for the Regional Animal 
Control Officer Inter Municipal Agreement (IMA) between the towns of Blackstone, Douglas, Hopedale, Mendon, Millville, Uxbridge

FY2028 Budget discussion- (slides presented will be attached for final records). Town Manager Cyganiewicz provides the following:  
FY26 are unaudited results as they are still closing out the fiscal year with DOR. FY26 was a very good year between excess revenue 
and turn back on the town side. Local receipts are where the largest number came from and property tax is also very strong. Excise tax
is the largest local receipt. The town turned back around $435,000 to the general fund from various departments. Net changes to the 
FY26 budget totaled + $1,600,193. Going forward we have made adjustments- for the FY28 Revenue estimates we adjusted local 
receipts to be more realistic (FY26 $2.56 M budgeted but $4.24M was received), Recurring cost pressure- snow & ice, out of district 
SPED, OPEB, Police & landfill services exceeded what was appropriated. Investment earnings continue to be tied to the economy – 
we will continue to monitor. FY28 Projected Revenue $42.84 M- Projected Expenses- $45.04M (projected gap is $2.2M). This is with
no supplemental transfers in to support the operational budget.  In review of the operating growth for FY28- education is showing a 
5.4% increase, employee benefits 14.6% increase, municipal depts..3.25% increase, pension 6.5 % increase and debt service shows a 
reduction of 11.2%. Health Insurance is looking like it will be a double digit increase (15%)- health insurance for town and school is 
covered under the town side- we pay 4 million in health ins- 3.1M of that is school, Educational expenses are increasing due to out of 
district tuition and employee contracts. The Teamsters and Police Union are going into contract negotiations. For projected revenue 
vs. expenses through 2033 there is an increase of $60 M in expenses and $55 M in revenue. In regards to options (best bang for buck) 
for closing the FY28 gap: use of reserves (one-time money), pursue an override which permanently raises the levy limit, reduce 
expenses by lowering the town and school budgets to align with available revenue or a combination by pairing use of reserves with 
reductions. Vice Chair Ettamarna feels we should see what the scenario looks like, just to make a good decision. What does a realistic 
live within our means scenario look like for FY28. Austin states you could do a combination and have slight deductions or you could 
use a little reserve. Reserves available once DOR certifies is 2.7M in free cash, the general stab. 3 M which requires 2/3 vote at town 
meeting, Health ins. Stab. 550,000- majority vote at town meeting and SPED stab 400,000. also a majority vote at town meeting. 
There are 2 structural levers- override or reductions- under expense reductions Austin shows a 50/50 spilt in terms of educational and 
municipal at 1.1M with cuts to the town (11.4%) and the school (3.9%). Austin says on the town side we are already lean on staffing 
and supplies & services. When asked where cuts would be taken on the town side- Austin replies there are still core essential services 
we have to provide but a 1.1 M reduction on a 10M budget would be a huge chunk- there would be a reduction in services. Select. 
Watkins asks if that would be reduced office hours? Austin replies potentially- if that is the direction the board wants him to look at he
will talk to Depts. about what those cuts would look like for each dept. Austin asks for direction from the board at this time. Vice 
Chair Ettamarna says 1.7M of the increase is driven by school vs trying to split a 2.2 to 1.1each. It may not be right to split the 2.2 by 
50/50. Jim is just trying to look at it the reasonable way. Chairperson Anderson states in our own lives we have cash reserves we try to
maintain- tough times come and we make cuts as to how much we use out of cash reserves so as not to draw down too quickly. We are
going to have to reinvent how we perform government, how we deliver services and what that looks like. Even with an override I do 
not see how we fix it. Jonathan thinks it will be a combination of using reserves, making cuts- how will be provide and deliver our 
services. The board is not ready to look at an override for FY28 if there is consensus to look at for FY29 Austin will look into that. 
Select. Limanek states that will give us time to look at what our costs and revenue look like- we may see something that adds revenue 
in and skew the numbers. Jesse thinks we should look at a combination approach for short term so it won’t hurt any approach 
significantly. We may have to look at reducing services, hours, staff and tapping reserves to a degree in a responsible way. No one 
approach is going to get us 2.2 million dollars.  Chair Anderson agrees and says that it is just principles of financial management. 
Select. Spengler feels the whole model needs to be rethought- no override will sustain us unless we go back every couple of years and 
no one will vote for it.  Select. Watkins says this projection did not include anything from the feasibility fire study. Or any of the 
issues we are having with some of our buildings. Austin wraps up the discussion saying there is consensus for the combination 
approach so reductions in use of reserves, is there cap of how much reserves. Select Limanek questions what the Capital plan looks 
like- Austin says the last few years it’s been 2M and that supports most depts.  Vice Chair Ettamarna says it is painful to have to make 
cuts if we were not to provide the money from Capital reserves. We need to see what that would look like. In regards to using reserves
Jims personal sentiment is it makes sense to provide the reserves. He hates draining down our reserves and it will put us in a spot next 
year for the one time things which then we would have to pass a big override or make some really big painful cuts. He doesn’t like 
doing that in a non-planful way. What do we do between now and then, what are the 2 different options. Jim thinks of more 
regionalization- kudos to Austin and other colleagues for things such as inter municipal agreements- there’s something more 
fundamental we can do to change the cost structure in the town. He also states it is sensible to use our reserves. Jim does not know if it
should be 50/50 or be more proportional to the cost drivers. Discussion continues- reduce levels of the special 2 stabilization funds by 
50% to be used for the purpose they are designed for – if there is a gap needed to be filled use some of the free cash. Jesse is not 
comfortable draining these two accounts down to zero. When asked the fund balance of free cash- Town Mgr. Cyganiewicz replies 
once the revenue and expense is turned back we will have 2.7M. Select. Watkins asks when was the last time we used general 
stabilization funds? Select. Limanek states that was created when we had the last crash, the purpose was if we suffer another 
significant hit that is the break glass in case of absolute emergency. Austin states that fund is not just for operating budgets but for 
unforeseen infrastructure or capital emergencies. Austin states ok- drain both funds down by 50%- are you looking to fill the 2.2 gap 
by 50% with reserves and then reductions? The breakdown- $225,000. from the health ins. fund and $200,000. From SPED Fund – we
need to come up with another $700,000. From free cash- that gets us to 2 million. Select Limanek replies tap the reserve funds for half
www.suttonma.gov
of the projected deficit and then wait and see what the real numbers come in and then we make our hard cuts or decisions but we are 
still looking for reductions. 
Economic Development discussion- Chairperson Anderson says this ties in to previous discussion but also this board for the last year 
has been trying to understand better what our role is and align with what state law and our own bylaws and Charter hold. We built a 
framework document for us to run by. This gives us a better understanding of what our day to day and how we are supposed to operate
and what our boundaries are.  One of the roles of the Select Board is Strategic Planning – we can set some guard rails but we can’t do 
that on our own. We need to look at how we work with other boards for things like economic development and housing and work with
these boards to put together a strategic plan that meets the town’s needs. Looking at the long term deficit from previous discussion we 
have to figure out how to solve for this. The problem is in looking at growth- the more you grow the more services you need. Jonathan
feels we need to meet with Planning and the ZBA to start discussions. Vice Chair Ettamarna feels economic development really 
impacts the budget and the revenue. The challenges on the cost side- what if there is a way to grow our revenue that does not 
significantly increase our cost. With growth the cost of services come along with it- but if there was a cluster of commercial 
enterprises that could help increase our revenue and not increase the cost that would help fix the curves. Also if we think about the 
culture of what Sutton is like to live in- the businesses in town matter greatly as well as preserving the farms. It’s important to 
preserve the nature of Sutton. Helping out small business opportunities would also be beneficial. To wrap it up- revenue for the town 
& preserving the character of the town is important. A later priority would be around jobs. Select. Limanek says we have a limited 
amount of parcels that are commercial zoned. Another thing- when a business is looking at possibility of coming into a town they 
watch board meetings – they make their decisions on that. Some of the conversations our boards have had could be a detractor. If we 
are looking for a business to come in and help fill the gap, we cannot be picking and choosing the type of businesses we may be 
comfortable with. If someone wants to invest in a business in town and it is not going to draw too much on water, our first responders, 
added students at the school: that’s kind of what we need more than anything. Jesse remains cautious because we could set a tone that 
businesses say forget about Sutton and that would be more detrimental then anything that we could achieve by collaboration. Jesse 
would like to be known as a business friendly town. Select. Watkins informs the board that the recent increase in draw on water in 
Wilks. has already attracted several interested candidates. There are already several queued up- once they get the ok from the water 
district they will be coming before planning and zoning. One is a big box store and the other is a the 40B with Galaxy (33000 sq. ft. of
retail and 310 apartments). These 2 projects will use almost the entire increase in the draw. This will leave us again with no water. Jen 
has worked to try and get in Bio and the issue has been no water. Christine attended a recent CMRPC meeting- Worcester is one of the
largest cities seeing growth in Biomed in the country. Jen Hager- Planning- states a business has to have an initial positive service 
letter from the water company for them to file with planning. Select Spengler states you are going to have more projects that are 
drawing more on our services and requiring more services.  The Select Board continue this discussion and will have a meeting with 
Planning Board and Zoning in the near future. 
Approve and sign the Warrant for the 2026 State Election -   Select Spengler motions to Approve & Sign the 2026 State Election 
Warrant- Select Limanek 2nds passes 5-0 with roll call vote- Limanek “aye” Watkins “aye”, Ettamarna “aye”, Spengler “aye” 
Anderson “aye”.
Town Manager Update:
 Amazon Prime air service- Austin attended the meeting a few weeks ago- there is a proposal for a drone to deliver items 
under 5lbs using a drone. It would include a small area in Sutton. The warehouse is located on Otis St in Westboro and the 
flight plan is to go 7.5 miles away. This is an opt in program and only available too single family homes. Approval from the 
host jurisdiction is needed (Westboro). This is an autonomous device. 
 Finance Committee closed their hearings for Town Meeting and approved all articles.
 CMRPC meeting for Hazardous Mitigation planning- Sutton rec. $35,000. Grant- the existing plan expired in 2021.
Select Board Round Table
Select Limanek reminds all of Waters Farm Day next week. He will be at the Sr. Center on 10/19 for Coffee with the Seniors.
The needs of the Food pantry are read along with the locations of drop off.
Vice Chair Ettamarna gives a shout out to Waters Farm Days and suggests volunteering.
Chair Anderson mentions the correspondence from Senator Fattman and State Rep McKenna regarding the Amazon Air 
delivery as well as correspondence from Jeffrey Hamill for ideas & thoughts on the drone discussion.
